principles.statement: Functions should do one thing and do it well.
principles.rationale: A function with a single responsibility is easier to name, test, and reuse; mixed responsibilities force callers to accept side effects they didn't ask for.

principles.statement: Names should reveal intent without needing a comment to explain them.
principles.rationale: A reader should be able to understand what a variable or function is for from its name alone.

principles.statement: Don't repeat yourself (DRY) — duplicated logic should be extracted to one place.
principles.rationale: Duplicated logic drifts out of sync over time; a bug fixed in one copy silently remains in the others.

heuristics.name: Single Responsibility Check
heuristics.description: If you can't describe what a function does in one short sentence without using 'and', it's doing too much.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Reviewing any function longer than ~15-20 lines, or any function whose name contains 'and'/'or'.
examples: A function named process_and_save_and_notify should likely be split into process, save, and notify.

heuristics.name: Comment Smell
heuristics.description: A comment that explains WHAT code does (rather than WHY) is a sign the code itself should be clearer.
examples: // increment counter above counter += 1 adds nothing; a comment explaining a non-obvious business rule is fine.

decision_rules.condition: A function has more than one clear, independent responsibility.
decision_rules.action: Flag it and recommend splitting it into separate single-purpose functions.
exceptions: Trivial glue/wrapper functions that just call the split-out pieces in sequence are fine.

decision_rules.condition: The same logic (not just similar-looking code, but the same rule) appears in more than one place.
decision_rules.action: Recommend extracting it into a shared function, method, or module.
exceptions: Coincidental similarity between unrelated pieces of logic that happen to look alike is not duplication.

decision_rules.condition: A name (variable, function, class) requires a comment to explain what it represents.
decision_rules.action: Recommend renaming it to something self-explanatory instead of relying on the comment.
